---
title: "Performance & Reliability"
---

IrisPipe separates **merge-gating regression tests** from long-running capacity benchmarks:

- **k6 Benchmark** ? API/runtime latency, 1k / 10k / 100k data-volume behavior, failure semantics, and PostgreSQL ? H2 coverage.
- **Backend K6 Checks** ? 10 regression suites against a real Spring Boot backend.
- **k6 Deep Volume Benchmark** ? scheduled/manual retained capacity snapshots.
- **Full RDBMS Matrix** ? six source-specific workflows covering H2, PostgreSQL, MySQL, MariaDB, SQL Server, and Oracle. A full run is 6 sources ? 6 destinations ? JOB/CHUNK ? 100K/1M/10M/20M/50M = **360 cases**.

## What the Benchmark Measures

The data-volume benchmark exercises real Spring Batch + JDBC execution and validates both throughput and data correctness:

1. Regular PR/main gate: H2 ? H2 JOB/CHUNK at 1k / 10k / 100k.
2. Failure semantics: a duplicate key on the final row proves the JOB vs CHUNK rollback boundary.
3. Cross-database correctness: destination row count must equal the expected row count; `COMPLETED` alone is not accepted as a pass.
4. Full matrix: every source can target every destination across H2 / PostgreSQL / MySQL / MariaDB / SQL Server / Oracle.
5. Capacity ladder: 100K / 1M / 10M / 20M / 50M for both JOB and CHUNK.

All numbers are repeatable GitHub-hosted-runner regression benchmarks, **not production-capacity claims**.

---

## JOB vs CHUNK: Transaction Boundary

The same `batchSize` has different transaction semantics:

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  subgraph JOB["JOB ? 50M rows"]
    J1["JDBC batches: 5,000 rows"] --> J2["1 destination transaction"] --> J3["Failure: rollback all 50M"]
  end
  subgraph CHUNK["CHUNK ? 50M rows"]
    C1["10,000 chunks ? 5,000 rows"] --> C2["10,000 independent commits"] --> C3["Failure: rollback only failing chunk"]
  end
```

| CI profile | `fetchSize` / `batchSize` | JOB transaction boundary | CHUNK transaction boundary |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Regular PR/main benchmark | 1,000 rows | One destination transaction for the whole job | Commit every 1,000 rows |
| Deep/full benchmark | 5,000 rows | One destination transaction for the whole job | Commit every 5,000 rows |

| Source rows | CHUNK transaction groups @ 5,000 | JOB transaction groups |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 100K | 20 | 1 |
| 1M | 200 | 1 |
| 10M | 2,000 | 1 |
| 20M | 4,000 | 1 |
| 50M | 10,000 | 1 |

The regular 10k failure test makes the trade-off observable. With a duplicate key on the final row and a 1,000-row batch, **JOB** rolls back all migrated rows and leaves only the pre-existing conflict row (**1 row**). **CHUNK** preserves the first nine committed chunks (**9,000 rows**) and rolls back only the failing tenth chunk, leaving **9,001 rows** including the pre-existing conflict.

---

## Benchmark Timing Boundary

Reported `duration_ms` / `rows_per_second` intentionally measure **IrisPipe migration execution**, not environment setup.

```{mermaid}
flowchart LR
  A["DB/container startup"] --> B["Source seed"] --> C["Backend startup"] --> D["Pipeline config"] --> E["START TIMER"] --> F["POST /sync-pipeline\nSpring Batch + JDBC + commits"] --> G["STOP TIMER"] --> H["Destination COUNT verification"] --> I["Publish report"]
```

**Included:** the synchronous `/api/v1/sync-pipeline` call from immediately before the request until the completed/failed response returns.

**Excluded:** database/container startup, source-data generation, backend startup/readiness, pipeline-config creation, post-run destination `COUNT(*)`, artifact aggregation, and Pages deployment.

This is why smaller cases can show lower rows/s: fixed Spring Batch / JDBC / transaction startup cost is amortized over fewer rows.

---

## Test Strategy

k6 is used for **integration-level correctness**, not only synthetic load generation. Each benchmark boots the actual backend, creates a real pipeline, executes JDBC migration, verifies runtime status, and validates persisted destination rows.

For external databases, source data is generated **inside the database before the timer starts**. The full matrix uses separate source and destination containers for cross-engine paths; same-engine paths use separate source/destination tables in the same engine instance.

---

## CI / Benchmark Triggering

Long-running 50M tests never block normal PR merges or ordinary `main` Pages deployment.

```{mermaid}
flowchart TD
  PR["PR / main push"] --> G["Unit tests + regular k6 gates"]
  G --> P["Deploy Quarto using retained benchmark JSON"]

  T["tag: benchmark-full-*"] --> H2["Source H2 ? 60 cases"]
  T --> PG["Source PostgreSQL ? 60 cases"]
  T --> MY["Source MySQL ? 60 cases"]
  T --> MA["Source MariaDB ? 60 cases"]
  T --> MS["Source SQL Server ? 60 cases"]
  T --> OR["Source Oracle ? 60 cases"]

  M["Manual: Full RDBMS Benchmark - All Sources"] --> H2
  M --> PG
  M --> MY
  M --> MA
  M --> MS
  M --> OR

  H2 --> R["Serial merge into retained deep-performance-results.json"]
  PG --> R
  MY --> R
  MA --> R
  MS --> R
  OR --> R
  R --> D["repository_dispatch ? GitHub Pages"]
```

A source-specific tag such as `benchmark-postgres-*` triggers only that source workflow; `benchmark-full-*` triggers all six source workflows.

The retained result file uses a merge key of `(db_pair, atomic_level, mode, row_count, batch_size)`. A normal merge to `main` **does not regenerate or clear deep results**, and a source-specific benchmark update replaces only the cases it actually measured.

---

## Benchmark Methodology

1. `mvn package` runs backend unit tests before benchmark execution.
2. Regular PR/main gates stay bounded; 10M+ capacity work is tag/manual/scheduled only.
3. Full matrix jobs use `batchSize=5,000` and validate 100K / 1M / 10M / 20M / 50M.
4. Source seed happens before the migration timer; k6 does not insert the benchmark dataset row-by-row.
5. External destination row counts are verified after the timer and must equal the expected count.
6. Benchmark snapshots are merged into retained history instead of replacing unrelated source/destination results.
